content:
Thunderbird for Android, like other Android apps, normally uses the "Contacts" app that is built in to Android. But you may need to give Thunderbird permission to access that app. You may have skipped giving Thunderbird the permissions it needed to access your Contacts when you set it up.

I think there is also a checkbox in the Thunderbird settings that tells Thunderbird to use your Contacts. And I think if you check that off, then it will prompt you to grant Thunderbird the permissions it requires to do this.

For many years, this request/bug has been marked as ignored/will not fix/not an issue. Honestly, when I saw the announcement for Thunderbird Pro, this was the first thing I thought of that will cause issues.

I have tried for many years to use Thunderbird as a replacement for my usual work email, and this is the biggest issue that prevents me from sticking with it 100%. There are multiple suggestions in these forums and reddit to simply tell Thunderbird to "add a copy of the sent email in the Inbox folder" but then I have double storage for no reason, and also something that every other mail client/service handles perfectly except for Thunderbird.

Thunderbird devs, you would do well to ask people of multiple use cases on how they use Thunderbird and what hurts their daily usage, if you want to ask people to invest and support Thunderbird & Thunderbird Pro. If this is missing from Thunderbird Pro and you get an influx of new users that will immediately notice this, it will cause a massive negative image that is tough to fix.
